title: Introductory Microbiology — Bacteria and Viruses
topicTitle: Monera: General introduction, structure of bacterial cell, mode of nutrition, bacterial growth; cyanobacteria (blue green algae); Virus: General introduction, structure and importance of virus, bacteriophage
notes: **Bacteria:** prokaryotic, no nucleus, cell wall of peptidoglycan (Gram-positive thick, Gram-negative thin with outer membrane). Shapes: cocci, bacilli, spirilla, vibrio.
**Bacterial cell structure:** cell wall, plasma membrane, cytoplasm, nucleoid (circular DNA), ribosomes (70S), plasmids (extrachromosomal DNA), capsule, flagella, pili.
**Nutrition:** autotrophic (photoautotrophs, chemoautotrophs) and heterotrophic (saprophytic, parasitic, symbiotic).
**Bacterial growth:** binary fission. Lag phase → log/exponential phase → stationary phase → death phase. Affected by temperature, pH, oxygen, nutrients.
**Cyanobacteria:** photosynthetic prokaryotes with chlorophyll a and phycocyanin. Fix nitrogen (heterocysts in Anabaena). Form blooms in eutrophic water. Examples: Nostoc, Anabaena, Oscillatoria.
**Virus:** acellular, obligate intracellular parasite. Structure: nucleic acid core (DNA or RNA) + protein coat (capsid) + sometimes lipid envelope.

**Bacteriophage:** virus that infects bacteria. T2 phage has icosahedral head, contractile tail. Lytic cycle: attachment, penetration, replication, assembly, lysis. Lysogenic cycle: phage DNA integrates into bacterial chromosome as prophage.
